simple.meaning: גָּוַע (gâvaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to breathe out , i.e. (by implication) expire.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 24 times in Genesis, Numbers, Joshua, Job, Psalms, and 2 more, beginning at Genesis 6:17. The surrounding contexts include family line, death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּוַע (H1478) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּוַע (gâvaʻ) / H1478 is traced through Genesis 6:17, Genesis 7:21, Genesis 25:8, Genesis 25:17 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to breathe out , i.e. (by implication) expire
definitions.usage: die, be dead, give up the ghost, perish.
definitions.full: H1478. gava גָּוַע verb expire perish, die (compare Arabic be empty, hungry ) — Qal Perfect גָּוַע Num 20:29 ; Josh 22:20 גָּוָ֑עוּ Lam 1:19 גָּוַעְנוּ Numbers 17:27; Num 20:3 ; Imperfect יִגְוַע Job 34:15 , יִגְוָ֑ע Gen 6:17 , יִגְוְעוּ Job 36:12 , יִגְוָע֑וּ Zech 13:8 , יִגְוָע֑וּן Psa 104:28 etc.; Infinitive construct גְּוַע Num 20:3 גְּוֺעַ Numbers 17:28; Participle גֹּוֵעַ Psa 88:16 ; — expire and die, only P & poetry; ׳ג וימת Gen 25:8 , 17 ; 35:29 (all P); || מות Job 3:11 ; 14:10 compare Numbers 17:28 (P); || אבד Numbers 17:27 we expire, we perish (P); || עָנִי Psa 88:15 (progressive parall.) distressed and about to die ; || אבותיו אל יאסף Gen 49:33 ; || ישׁוב עלעֿפר Job 34:15 compare Psa 104:29 ; || יִכָּֽרְתוּ Zech 13:8 ; absolute, both prose and (especially) poetry Num 20:3 (twice in verse); 20:29 ; Josh 22:20 ; Gen 6:17 ; 7:21 (all P) Job 10:13 ; 13:19 ; 27:5 ; 36:12 ; Lam 1:19 ; Job 29:18 אגוע עִםקִֿנִּי with my nest shall I die , i.e. in full possession of what is mine, compare Di.

occurrences.englishText: I, even I, will bring the flood of waters on this earth, to destroy all flesh having the breath of life from under the sky. Everything that is in the earth will die.
All flesh died that moved on the earth, including birds, livestock, animals, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and every man.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
These are the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years. He gave up his spirit and died, and was gathered to his people.
Isaac gave up the spirit and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.
When Jacob finished charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, breathed his last breath, and was gathered to his people.
The people quarreled with Moses, and spoke, saying, “We wish that we had died when our brothers died before Yahweh!
The people quarreled with Moses, and spoke, saying, “We wish that we had died when our brothers died before Yahweh!
When all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they wept for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
Didn’t Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the devoted thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel? That man didn’t perish alone in his iniquity.’ ”
“Why didn’t I die from the womb?
“ ‘Why, then, have you brought me out of the womb?
Who is he who will contend with me?
But man dies, and is laid low.
Far be it from me that I should justify you.
Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house,
all flesh would perish together,
But if they don’t listen, they will perish by the sword;
Your fierce wrath has gone over me.
You hide your face; they are troubled.
“I called for my lovers,
It shall happen that in all the land,” says Yahweh,
